title: Chapter 27 — Procellariiformes
description: Tubenoses — seabirds defined by their prominent nasal passages (tubenose) that excrete excess salt. This order includes the petrels, shearwaters, storm petrels, and albatrosses. They are masterful long-distance flyers, covering entire ocean basins on their migrations. Many species nest in burrows on remote islands and only return to land under cover of darkness. The order ranges from the tiny 20-gram European Storm Petrel to the wandering albatross with its 3.5-metre wingspan.

children.name: Fulmarus glacialis
children.description: The northern fulmar, Arctic fulmar, Fulmars come in one of two colour morphs; a light one in temperate populations, with white head and body and grey wings and tail, and a dark one in arctic populations, which is uniformly grey; intermediate birds are common.

children.name: Fulmarus glacialoides
children.description: The southern fulmar (Fulmarus glacialoides) is a seabird of the Southern Hemisphere.

children.name: Pagodroma nivea
children.description: The snow petrel (Pagodroma nivea) is the only member of the genus Pagodroma.

children.name: Thalassoica antarctica
children.description: The Antarctic petrel (Thalassoica antarctica) is a boldly marked dark brown and white petrel, found in Antarctica, most commonly in the Ross and Weddell Seas.

children.name: Daption capense
children.description: The pintado petrel (Daption capense), also called the Cape petrel, or Cape fulmar, is a common seabird of the Southern Ocean from the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Aphrodroma brevirostris
children.description: thumb| Aphrodroma brevirostris - [[MHNT]].

children.name: Puffinus puffinus
children.description: The Manx shearwater (Puffinus puffinus) is a medium-sized shearwater in the seabird family Procellariidae.

children.name: Puffinus mauretanicus
children.description: The Balearic shearwater (Puffinus mauretanicus) is a medium-sized shearwater in the seabird family Procellariidae.

children.name: Puffinus yelkouan
children.description: thumb|upright=0.8|Egg of the yelkouan shearwater.

children.name: Puffinus lherminieri
children.description: The Sargasso shearwater (Puffinus lherminieri) is a small tropical seabird in the petrel family.

children.name: Puffinus bailloni
children.description: The tropical shearwater (Puffinus bailloni) is a seabird in the family Procellariidae formerly considered conspecific with Audubon's shearwater (Puffinus lherminieri).

children.name: Puffinus baroli
children.description: The Barolo shearwater (Puffinus baroli), also known as the North Atlantic little shearwater or Macaronesian shearwater, is a small shearwater which breeds in the Azores and Canaries of Macaronesia in the North Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Puffinus nativitatis
children.description: The Christmas shearwater or ao ū (Puffinus nativitatis) is a medium-sized shearwater of the tropical Central Pacific.

children.name: Puffinus gavia
children.description: The fluttering shearwater (Puffinus gavia) is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Puffinus myrtae
children.description: The Rapa shearwater (Puffinus myrtae), is a rare seabird of the tropics from the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Puffinus assimilis
children.description: The little shearwater (Puffinus assimilis) is a small shearwater in the petrel family Procellariidae.

children.name: Puffinus elegans
children.description: The subantarctic shearwater (Puffinus elegans) is a small bird species which breeds in Tristan da Cunha, islands of the southern Indian Ocean and New Zealand Subantarctic Islands.

children.name: Calonectris leucomelas
children.description: The streaked shearwater (Calonectris leucomelas) is a species of seabird in the petrel family Procellariidae.

children.name: Ardenna gravis
children.description: The great shearwater (Ardenna gravis) is a large shearwater in the seabird family Procellariidae.

children.name: Ardenna bulleri
children.description: Buller's shearwater is a Pacific species of seabird in the family Procellariidae; it is also known as the grey-backed shearwater or New Zealand shearwater. A member of the black-billed wedge-tailed Thyellodroma group, among the larger shearwaters of the genus Ardenna, it forms a superspecies with the wedge-tailed shearwater.

children.name: Ardenna grisea
children.description: The sooty shearwater (Ardenna grisea) is a medium-large shearwater in the seabird family Procellariidae.

children.name: Pterodroma heraldica
children.description: The Herald petrel (Pterodroma heraldica) is a species of seabird and a member of the gadfly petrels.

children.name: Pterodroma solandri
children.description: The providence petrel (Pterodroma solandri) is a large and heavy build gadfly petrel that nests in two locations in the Tasman Sea: Lord Howe Island (some 800 km from the Australian mainland) and Philip Island.

children.name: Pterodroma brevipes
children.description: The collared petrel (Pterodroma brevipes) is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Pterodroma sandwichensis
children.description: The Hawaiian petrel or ua u (Pterodroma sandwichensis) is a large, dark grey-brown and white petrel that is endemic to Hawai i.

children.name: Pterodroma cahow
children.description: The Bermuda petrel (Pterodroma cahow) is a gadfly petrel.

children.name: Pterodroma deserta
children.description: The Desertas petrel (Pterodroma deserta) is a small seabird in the gadfly petrel genus which breeds on Bugio Island in the Desertas off Madeira.

children.name: Pterodroma incerta
children.description: The Atlantic petrel (Pterodroma incerta) is a gadfly petrel endemic to the South Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Pterodroma mollis
children.description: The soft-plumaged petrel is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Pterodroma neglecta
children.description: The Kermadec petrel is a species of gadfly petrel in the family Procellariidae. It is 38 cm long with a wingspan of 100 cm. It is polymorphic, with light, dark and intermediate morphs known.

children.name: Pterodroma atrata
children.description: The Henderson petrel (Pterodroma atrata) is a ground-nesting species of gadfly petrel in the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Pterodroma inexpectata
children.description: Procellaria raolensis Bonaparte, 1857 (nomen novum).

children.name: Pterodroma magentae
children.description: The magenta petrel (Pterodroma magentae), or Chatham Island tāiko, is a small seabird in the gadfly petrel genus, Pterodroma.

children.name: Pterodroma defilippiana
children.description: Masatierra petrel (Pterodroma defilippiana) or De Filippi's petrel, is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Pterodroma alba
children.description: Procellaria alba Gmelin, 1789 Procellaria parvirostris Peale, 1848 Rhantistes parvirostris Bp, 1856 Æstrelata parvirostris Coues, 1866 Œstrelata parvirostris Lister, 1891.

children.name: Pterodroma arminjoniana
children.description: | range_map = Pterodroma arminjoniana map.svg.

children.name: Pterodroma hypoleuca
children.description: The Bonin petrel or nunulu (Pterodroma hypoleuca) is a seabird in the family Procellariidae.

children.name: Pterodroma occulta
children.description: The Vanuatu petrel or Falla's petrel (Pterodroma occulta) is a species of gadfly petrel.

children.name: Procellaria cinerea
children.description: The grey petrel (Procellaria cinerea), also called the gray petrel, brown petrel, pediunker or grey shearwater, is a species of seabird in the Procellariidae, or petrel family.

children.name: Procellaria conspicillata
children.description: The spectacled petrel (Procellaria conspicillata) is a rare seabird that nests only on the high western plateau of Inaccessible Island in the South Atlantic Tristan da Cunha group.

children.name: Procellaria parkinsoni
children.description: The black petrel (Procellaria parkinsoni), ( , or ) also called Parkinson's petrel, is a medium-sized, black-plumaged petrel, the smallest of the Procellaria.

children.name: Procellaria westlandica
children.description: The Westland petrel (Procellaria westlandica), (), also known as the Westland black petrel, is a moderately large seabird in the petrel family Procellariidae, that is endemic to New Zealand.

children.name: Pseudobulweria rostrata
children.description: The Tahiti petrel (Pseudobulweria rostrata) is a medium-sized, dark brown and white seabird found across the Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Pseudobulweria macgillivrayi
children.description: The Fiji petrel (Pseudobulweria macgillivrayi), also known as MacGillivray's petrel, is a small, dark gadfly petrel.

children.name: Pseudobulweria aterrima
children.description: The Mascarene petrel (Pseudobulweria aterrima) is a medium-sized, dark petrel.

children.name: Pachyptila desolata
children.description: The Antarctic prion (Pachyptila desolata) also known as the dove prion, or totorore in Māori, is the largest of the prions, a genus of small petrels of the Southern Ocean.

children.name: Pachyptila turtur
children.description: The fairy prion (Pachyptila turtur) is a small seabird with the standard prion plumage of blue-grey upperparts with a prominent dark "M" marking and white underneath.

children.name: Pachyptila crassirostris
children.description: The fulmar prion (Pachyptila crassirostris) is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae, found in the southern oceans.

children.name: Halobaena caerulea
children.description: thumb|Holding a blue petrel during a [[Bird ringing|ringing campaign]].

children.name: Pelecanoides magellani
children.description: The Magellanic diving petrel (Pelecanoides magellani) is a species of diving petrel, one of five very similar, small, auk-like petrels found exclusively in the southern oceans.

children.name: Fregetta
children.description: Fregetta — a genus of northern storm petrels in the family Hydrobatidae.

children.name: Fregetta grallaria
children.description: The white-bellied storm petrel is a species of seabird in the family Oceanitidae. It is found in Angola, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, French Polynesia, French Southern Territories, Maldives, Namibia, New Zealand, Perú, Saint Helena, and South Africa. Its natural habitat is open seas.

children.name: Fregetta tropica
children.description: The black-bellied storm petrel is a species of seabird in the family Oceanitidae.

children.name: Garrodia
children.description: Garrodia — a genus of northern storm petrels in the family Hydrobatidae.

children.name: Garrodia nereis
children.description: The grey-backed storm petrel is a species of seabird in the austral storm petrel family Oceanitidae. It is monotypic within the genus Garrodia. It is found in Antarctica, Argentina, Australia, Chile, Falkland Islands, French Southern Territories, New Zealand, Saint Helena, South Africa, and South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.

children.name: Hydrobates
children.description: Storm petrels — tiny, bat-like seabirds that patter across the ocean surface with their feet, picking plankton from the water. They are the smallest seabirds in the world, some species weighing as little as 20 grams. Their name comes from their habit of appearing in the lee of ships during storms. They nest in burrows or rock crevices on islands, returning to land only at night.

children.name: Hydrobates pelagicus
children.description: The European storm petrel (Hydrobates pelagicus), also known as British storm petrel, or just storm petrel, is a species of seabird in the northern storm petrel family, Hydrobatidae.

children.name: Hydrobates homochroa
children.description: The ashy storm petrel (Hydrobates homochroa) is a small, scarce seabird of the storm petrel family Hydrobatidae.

children.name: Pelagodroma
children.description: Pelagodroma — a genus of northern storm petrels in the family Hydrobatidae.

children.name: Pelagodroma marina
children.description: The white-faced storm petrel, also known as white-faced petrel or frigate petrel, is a small seabird of the austral storm petrel family Oceanitidae. It is the only member of the monotypic genus Pelagodroma. It is widely distributed across the northern and southern hemisphere, especially around the coastal and open ocean waters of southern Australia, New Zealand, Tristan da Cunha, Cabo Verde, the Canary islands and the Selvagens islands.

children.name: Diomedea
children.description: The great albatrosses — the largest seabirds on Earth, with the longest wingspans of any living bird. The Wandering Albatross can reach a wingspan of 3.7 metres. These ocean wanderers spend most of their lives in flight, covering thousands of kilometres over the Southern Ocean using dynamic soaring. They return to land only to breed, forming lifelong pair bonds.

children.name: Diomedea exulans
children.description: The snowy albatross is one of the two largest members of the genus Diomedea (the great albatrosses), being similar in size to the southern royal albatross.

children.name: Diomedea amsterdamensis
children.description: The Amsterdam albatross or Amsterdam Island albatross More recently, mitochondrial DNA comparisons between the Amsterdam albatross, the wandering albatross Diomedea exulans, the Antipodean albatross D. antipodensis and the Tristan albatross D. dabbenena, provide clear genetic evidence that the Amsterdam albatross is a separate species.

children.name: Diomedea antipodensis
children.description: The Antipodean albatross (Diomedea antipodensis) ( ) is a large seabird in the albatross family.

children.name: Phoebastria
children.description: Phoebastria — a genus of albatrosses in the family Diomedeidae.

children.name: Phoebastria albatrus
children.description: The short-tailed albatross or Steller's albatross is a large rare seabird from the North Pacific. Although related to the other North Pacific albatrosses, it also exhibits behavioural and morphological links to the albatrosses of the Southern Ocean. It was described by the German naturalist Peter Simon Pallas from skins collected by Georg Wilhelm Steller.

children.name: Phoebastria immutabilis
children.description: The Laysan albatross is a large seabird that ranges across the North Pacific. The Northwestern Hawaiian Islands are home to 99.7% of the population. This small gull-like albatross is the second-most common seabird in the Hawaiian Islands, with an estimated population of 1.18 million birds, and is currently expanding its range to new islands.

children.name: Phoebastria irrorata
children.description: The waved albatross, also known as Galapagos albatross, is one of three species of the family Diomedeidae that occur in the tropics. When they forage, they follow a straight path to a single site off the coast of Peru, about 1,000 km (620 mi) to the east. During the non-breeding season, these birds reside primarily on the Ecuadorian and Peruvian coasts.

children.name: Phoebastria nigripes
children.description: The black-footed albatross is a large seabird of the albatross family Diomedeidae from the North Pacific. All but 2.5% of the population is found among the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands. It is one of three species of albatross that range in the Northern Hemisphere, nesting on isolated tropical islands.

children.name: Phoebetria
children.description: Sooty albatrosses — distinctive dark-plumaged albatrosses with long, wedge-shaped tails and a more gull-like flight. Found exclusively in the Southern Ocean. Their dark plumage may serve as camouflage against the dark seas of the stormy latitudes they inhabit.

children.name: Thalassarche
children.description: The mollymawks — medium-sized albatrosses with black-and-white plumage and brightly coloured bills. They are the most numerous and widespread albatrosses, often following ships for extended periods. Several species are threatened by longline fishing.

children.name: Thalassarche cauta
children.description: thumb|right|Over pelagic waters off the southeast coast of Tasmania.

children.name: Thalassarche chrysostoma
children.description: The grey-headed albatross also known as the gray-headed mollymawk, is a large seabird from the albatross family. It has a circumpolar distribution, nesting on isolated islands in the Southern Ocean and feeding at high latitudes, further south than any of the other mollymawks. Its name derives from its ashy-gray head, throat and upper neck.

children.name: Thalassarche eremita
children.description: thumb|Eaglehawk Neck, Tasmania thumb|Eaglehawk Neck, Tasmania.

children.name: Thalassarche impavida
children.description: The Campbell albatross (Thalassarche impavida) or Campbell mollymawk is a medium-sized mollymawk in the albatross family.

children.name: Oceanites
children.description: Small, sooty-brown storm petrels with a conspicuous white rump and pale underwing bar. They patter on the water surface with a distinctive fluttering flight, feeding on plankton and small fish. The genus includes Wilson's Storm Petrel, one of the most abundant and widely distributed seabirds on Earth.

children.name: Oceanites pincanus
children.description: A recently described storm petrel from the coastal waters of Chile, named after the Pincoya, a mythical sea spirit from Chiloé folklore. It is similar to Wilson's Storm Petrel but has a longer tail and different vocalisations. Its breeding grounds were only discovered in 2021 in the coastal mountains of southern Chile.

children.name: Garrodia
children.description: A monotypic genus of small storm petrel with a distinctive grey back and dark cap, giving it a hooded appearance. It breeds exclusively on islands in the Southern Ocean.

children.name: Pelagodroma
children.description: A monotypic genus of storm petrel with extraordinarily long legs that trail well beyond the tail in flight. The White-faced Storm Petrel has a distinctive appearance with a white face and dark eyestripe, resembling a tiny shearwater.

children.name: Fregetta
children.description: Storm petrels with a distinctive white belly variably streaked with dark, contrasting with a sooty-black head and upperparts. They breed on remote islands in the Southern Ocean and tropical Atlantic, foraging widely in pelagic waters.

children.name: Nesofregetta
children.description: A monotypic genus of large, strikingly patterned storm petrel found in the tropical Pacific Ocean. It is the largest storm petrel in the Southern Ocean and has a distinctive white collar and breast band.
